answer: Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. Work waits on the echo until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the relic of the next round. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, burned when the recruit misbehaves. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the kernel of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
